speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our assessment, how long has this dizziness been occurring, and is it constant or does it come in episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The fact that the spinning sensation lasted only about 3 minutes and has since resolved is highly suggestive of a specific inner ear mechanism. To narrow this down, did the episode occur specifically when you changed your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of brief, episodic vertigo triggered by head position changes, accompanied by nausea and vomiting, is classic for this condition. Given the symptoms have resolved and you are at baseline, no immediate imaging or further tests are required. I recommend conservative management with head position avoidance and possibly the Epley maneuver. Please return if symptoms recur or if you experience new neurological deficits.
